main_body: A 4x3-tile patch of green ground with a repeating grass-tuft pattern, with a few orange dots. It is a flat terrain surface, not a standing object.
top_band: none (flat terrain pattern; the column scan shows only repeating mid-green and dark-green runs with no top/front structure)
evidence: The kind is terrain, so the 3/4 standing-object contract does not apply. The column scan shows only a repeating mid-green (L=86) and dark-green (L=64) pattern. There is no standing volume, no isometric side face and no elevation drawing. The ground reads as a flat top-down surface, which is correct for terrain.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 6 distinct colours in total and a median of 6 per tile. The grass reference has 80 colours and a median of 26 per tile. The candidate's ramp has about 3-4 greens, plus a few orange dots that read as odd, unmotivated accents. The grass tufts are the same stamp repeated on a rigid grid in every tile, which looks mechanical, whereas the Beodeul grass varies tile to tile with clumps and soil grain. There are no 5x5 flat fills and no neutral black outlines, which is fine. Even so, the shading depth and tile information are far below the grass reference, and the grass reference is the closest comparison for a green ground patch.
